name: crew
description: The orchestrator/worker session model over herdr or Orca, the project file's declared layer. An orchestrator session keeps its context for decisions and dispatches everything else to worker sessions launched by seat name: the operator's own files name each seat (~/.claude/crew/agents.md on the machine, .crew/roles.md in the project), implementers route by complexity class, one reviewer session runs its review command (/code-review by default) once per PR, the retained implementer works GitHub threads to zero; clean gates merge under a project standing order granting this role merge authority, else on the operator's word; operator gates and operator merge executors go to the operator. A session budget caps each work item at one implementer and one verifier. Each seat gets its own labelled tab holding one full-size pane, in the tree its --cwd names, so a run of five seats is five readable tabs. Readiness is derived, not declared: a seat herdr detects waits on a typed agent state, a seat it does not waits on a screen pattern, so an undetected agent CLI is a first-class seat and a detection manifest later upgrades it with no edit. A run's state lives in a dagr run.json; a small bash writer, bin/crew-run, takes the attempt transitions (open, settle, send-back) and any whole document (commit), each ending in dagr's check-then-rename loop, so a document the linter rejects never replaces the file. One fail-open hook tells a seat its own context figure past a configurable ceiling (default 500000 tokens) — a coordinator seat rotates on it, a leaf finishes; where molt runs, a child hands off to its parent and the top molts in place. Defers every other layer command to that layer's own guide. No lib; the writer keeps no state of its own.

context_ceiling.title: Context ceiling (tokens)
context_ceiling.description: Past this many tokens of context, a crew coordinator seat (the top, a spine session, a work-PR session) is told to finish the unit in hand, start no new one and rotate at its next boundary. 500000 is half a 1M window. Any number of 1 or more is accepted; a fractional setting fires at the next whole token, and an invalid or sub-1 value uses the default.
